title: Policy for trading in Company securities

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Directors, senior executives, employees and consultants of the Company. All substantive prohibitions (clearance, trading window, hedging of unvested plan securities) apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Company directors, distinguished for two extra disclosure duties: notifiable interest changes within 24 hours, and notification of margin loans or similar funding arrangements over the Company's securities.

windows.start_anchor: 24 hours after the holding of the AGM or any other general meeting, the announcement of annual or half-year results, the announcement of quarterly reports, or any other public ASX announcement (other than an Appendix 3Y)
windows.end_anchor: 10 business days after the window opens

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may notify a Relevant Person, if it is in possession of unpublished price sensitive information, that they may not trade during all or part of the trading window; confidentiality of this notification is not addressed. Outside the notified trading windows, the Chairman has discretion to grant clearance in exceptional circumstances (financial hardship, court order, or other overriding legal or statutory circumstance).

rules.detail: Put and call options and other derivative instruments over unvested plan securities are named examples of prohibited hedging arrangements.
rules.evidence: Directors, Officers and employees must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan.

rules.detail: A put/call option or other derivative over vested Securities is treated as hedging that 'must comply with this Policy', i.e. it is a trade requiring prior clearance from the Chairman or CEO and must occur inside a trading window (or under the Chairman's out-of-window discretion).
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements over unvested plan securities.
rules.evidence: Directors, Officers and employees must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities is permitted but must comply with the ordinary clearance and trading-window regime.
rules.evidence: In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy.

rules.detail: No mention of prepaid forwards, monetisation or similar structures.
Short selling is not named or otherwise addressed.
Securities lending is not named or otherwise addressed.
CFDs are not named; only put/call options and 'other derivative instruments' used for hedging purposes are addressed under clause 7.

Directors may enter a margin loan or similar funding arrangement over Company securities provided they notify the Company Secretary of it and of any variations, including the number of securities involved, the circumstances triggering margin calls, and the lender's right to dispose of securities. No prior approval is required, only notification.
rules.evidence: All directors must notify the Company Secretary of any margin loan or similar funding arrangement entered into in relation to the Company's securities and any variations to such arrangements, including the number of securities involved, the circumstances in which the lender can make margin calls, and the right of the lender to dispose of securities.

rules.detail: The clause 6 notification duty is expressed only for directors; no equivalent obligation or restriction is stated for other Relevant Persons.

Granting security to a margin lender is contemplated and permitted provided the director notifies the Company Secretary of the lender's right to dispose of the secured securities and the circumstances of margin calls.
rules.evidence: the right of the lender to dispose of securities

rules.detail: A margin loan or 'similar funding arrangement' secured on Company securities is permitted for directors subject only to notifying the Company Secretary at inception and on variation; no clearance or window restriction is stated for entering the financing itself.
rules.evidence: All directors must notify the Company Secretary of any margin loan or similar funding arrangement entered into in relation to the Company's securities and any variations to such arrangements

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or intention-based short-term dealing restriction.

clearance.approver: Chairman or Chief Executive (if the Chair is unavailable)
clearance.evidence: Clearance to trade must be received from the Chairman or Chief Executive (if the Chair is unavailable) prior to undertaking a trade. Clearance if received will apply for 5 business days from the date provided.

Within 24 hours of a director being appointed to the Board, resigning or being removed from the Board, or trading in the Company's securities, full details of the director's notifiable interests in the Company's securities and changes in such interest must be advised to the Company Secretary

exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances would include, but not be limited to cases of severe financial hardship
where court orders exist or other overriding legal or statutory circumstance requiring the sale or transfer of the securities.
The Share Trading policy does not apply where there is no change in beneficial interest in the securities.

financing_disclosure: Directors: at inception and on any variation of a margin loan or similar funding arrangement over Company securities, to the Company Secretary, disclosing number of securities, margin-call circumstances and the lender's disposal right; no deadline specified.

exemption_authority: Chairman (or CEO if Chair unavailable) may grant clearance to trade outside a trading window at their discretion, generally only in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, court orders or other overriding legal or statutory circumstance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following trades are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... 8.5 margin calls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's forced sale on a margin call falls entirely outside the policy, so a bank enforcing security under a funded collar can sell the collared shares without breaching the trading window or clearance rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All directors must notify the Company Secretary of any margin loan or similar funding arrangement entered into in relation to the Company's securities and any variations to such arrangements, including the number of securities involved, the circumstances in which the lender can make margin calls, and the right of the lender to dispose of securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not prohibited and does not require prior clearance for directors, only post-inception notification to the Company Secretary disclosing the lender's margin-call and disposal rights; other Relevant Persons have no equivalent stated obligation at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, Officers and employees must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can only be written over vested Securities; unvested plan securities cannot be the reference shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Within 24 hours of ... trading in the Company's securities, full details of the director's notifiable interests in the Company's securities and changes in such interest must be advised to the Company Secretary so that a record is kept within the Company and so that necessary ASX notifications can occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, or unwind of, the collar by a director must be reported to the Company Secretary within 24 hours for ASX notification purposes, in addition to any pre-trade clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons may trade in the Company's securities on ASX in the period of 10 business days commencing 24 hours following: the holding of the Annual General Meeting or any other General Meeting; the announcement of Annual or Half-Year results; the announcement of Quarterly Reports; and any other public announcement on ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This policy uses defined open trading windows rather than blackout periods; collar entry, unwind or roll must fall inside one of these 10-business-day windows (or be separately cleared by the Chairman under the exceptional-circumstances discretion) and clearance is only valid for 5 business days.

summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this policy, subject to standard trading controls. The derivative legs (put and call) over vested shares are treated as hedging that 'must comply with this Policy', meaning the Relevant Person needs prior clearance from the Chairman or CEO, executed within the 5-business-day clearance validity and inside a 10-business-day open trading window (or under the Chairman's exceptional-circumstances discretion), and not while holding unpublished price-sensitive information. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited: directors need only notify the Company Secretary of the margin loan or similar funding arrangement, its variations, the margin-call triggers and the lender's disposal rights, with no prior approval required; non-director employees have no stated obligation at all. Hedging of unvested plan securities is banned outright, so the collar can only be written over vested holdings. A lender's forced sale on a margin call is expressly excluded from the policy's operation, so the bank can enforce its security without breaching trading restrictions, and directors must still separately report the transaction to the Company Secretary within 24 hours for ASX purposes.
